items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: And do you know that I had something to do with him making records? Years later?

ctx.x: Speaking of that, when did you first hear the blues?

Oh, the first time I heard the blues was in Waco. A man had been...well the blues...in 1915, a black man had been lynched in a town called Robertsonville. I didn't pay any attention to the blues that much...this guy...because blues were considered vulgar and you couldn't sing it at home--sometime your father run you away from home, you had to leave home if you sang, you know, "Goin' Down to the River, Take a Rocking Chair." Well now, what had happened was...the song was...he had a parody. The parody was, "I never…

time,used to come to Waco and pick his big guitar and sing "Going Down to the River, Take a Rocking Chair/ The Blues overtake Me, Going to Rock Away From Here." And sang various blues that they make up. You know, in the black community, if a guy...if his woman left him to go up to [the] country, you know, he'd compose a song. Got a new pair of shoes, if he went to prison for ten years, they would create songs based on whatever the incident of the evening was. ....How are you running on?
